key_insight: The paper replaces interface-handling tricks in PINNs with a variational graph formulation that lets heterogeneity live in the mesh, not in the neural trial field.
engineering_relevance: This yields a penalty-free, label-free surrogate for heterogeneous solid mechanics that is robust to large stiffness contrasts and useful for parametric studies or inverse identification.
method: Builds a conforming adaptive mesh graph with element-wise constitutive laws.
Minimizes the discrete total potential energy, matching the FE Ritz functional for piecewise-linear elements.
Enforces Dirichlet boundary conditions by construction, avoiding interface weights and transition-width tuning.
evidence_signal: Across stiffness contrasts from E_inc/E_mat in [10^-2, 10^2], the PI-GNN kept von Mises error below 3.58% and outperformed strong-form/energy-based PINN baselines on displacement and stress error.
watch_item: Training is substantially more expensive than a single finite-element solve, so the method is best viewed as a surrogate or inverse-design tool rather than a replacement for one-off FE analysis.
paper_title: A variational physics-informed graph neural network for heterogeneous solid mechanics
